newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: World Bank officials on visit to Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: World Bank officials on visit to Belgrade.

text.p: World Bank officials have arrived in Belgrade on a fact finding mission on the Yugoslav economy, the first by the Bank in five years, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The delegation will present a report on how other central European economies have handled transition to a market economy, and point out the relevance this has for Yugoslavia.
It would also have a "discreet" meeting with the Yugoslav government and finance officials, the papers said.

The U.N. oil and trade embargo imposed in May 1992 for Belgrade's involvement in the Bosnian war has banned Yugoslavia from world finacial markets and institutions, such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.

The U.N. Security Council lifted the sanctions on October 1, but the so called "outer wall" of sanctions remained in place blocking Serbia and Montenegro, the two Yugoslav republics, from returning to the IMF and the World Bank.

The U.S. demands Yugoslavia improve its cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal and upgrade human rights especially in its southern province of Kosovo before it returns to the IMF and the Bank.
Analysts say Yugoslavia's cash-strapped economy urgently needs fresh foreign funds to kick-start its idle production or face collapse. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
